one_line: A shared architecture studio where a human and agent shape a live building model.
what_it_does: Lets users explore, edit, inspect, and validate an architectural design on a shared browser canvas.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to the live architectural model makes agent edits and inspection more precise than pixel-level UI driving, while the human and agent share the same design state.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly describes human and AI agent designing together on the same live canvas.
Frame sheet shows a morphing 3D building sequence and a separate editor with floor-plan blocks and property controls.
execution_rationale: The visual sequence shows a coherent architecture workflow from guided showcase to interactive floor-plan editing, with a plausible finished scope.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows progressive building assembly across multiple states.
Editor states show modal progression, canvas modules, sidebar, and numeric properties.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete accessibility problem for non-architects who want to explore and communicate a future home before professional design work.
impact_evidence: About text identifies room relationships, circulation, dimensions, and visualization as the target problem.
Finished multi-level house and editable plan are visible in the packet.
creativity_rationale: The human-agent co-design framing and morphing architectural model are a fresh, ambitious synthesis for the medium.
creativity_evidence: Same-live-building collaboration is central to the pitch.
Video frames present both evolving 3D massing and modular plan editing.
usability_note: The editor is visually structured, though the multi-stage architecture workflow may require guidance.
advance_reason: High-quality, clearly demonstrated shared design workflow with substantial WebMCP value.

one_line: A native WebMCP website-audit and migration-baseline workspace.
what_it_does: Inspects pages, discovers URLs, finds broken links, and creates structured migration plans for humans and agents.
leverage_rationale: Bounded inspection tools expose structured website facts directly to agents, avoiding unreliable visual navigation and making migration reconnaissance repeatable.
leverage_evidence: Five named native tools cover inspect_page, scan_site, list_pages, find_broken_links, and create_migration_plan.
Pitch describes a live activity panel showing actual tool calls and results.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a focused workflow with explicit safety constraints and a coherent audit-to-plan path; frames show the inspection product interface.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows repeated inspection UI with page-inspection section and surrounding status/tool panels.
About text specifies redirect validation, bounded sizes, traversal, and concurrency.
impact_rationale: Website migrations have a real, specific audience and costly failure modes around broken links, SEO metadata, and lost journeys.
impact_evidence: About text identifies migration teams and concrete reconnaissance risks.
Visible product headline and page-inspection workflow match the stated use case.
creativity_rationale: It is a well-targeted and thoughtfully agent-native application of WebMCP, though the underlying audit category is established.
creativity_evidence: Native tools are designed around migration actions rather than generic chat.
Shared human-agent inspection workspace is emphasized.
usability_note: Focused workflow and bounded actions suggest good usability; text is small in the frame evidence.
advance_reason: Concrete audience, strong WebMCP delta, and coherent product scope.

one_line: A browser-based queue and working-memory bridge between AI agents.
what_it_does: Lets one agent submit contextual tasks for another agent to claim, execute, and return through a shared queue.
leverage_rationale: The product directly uses the browser as an agent-to-agent coordination layer, preserving shared task state and context across otherwise isolated platforms.
leverage_evidence: Five WebMCP tools cover brief, submit_task, status, result, and remember.
Pitch explicitly frames the browser as dispatcher between ChatGPT and Claude Code or other agents.
execution_rationale: The frames show a coherent queue/workspace concept and task flow, but the submitted demo is marked dead and end-to-end worker completion is not fully visible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows task prompt, workspace, status areas, and result/task-style interfaces.
FACTS reports demo_alive=dead.
impact_rationale: It addresses a real coordination and context-transfer problem for users working across multiple AI platforms.
impact_evidence: About text describes repeated manual copy/paste between capable AI tools.
Visible queue and working-memory interface supports the stated workflow.
creativity_rationale: Using the page itself as an open coordination layer between competing agents is memorable and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Cross-platform agent handoff is the core concept.
The queue, memory, and result loop are pursued as a distinct product model.
usability_note: The flow appears understandable, but the dead live demo and dense task states reduce confidence in practical usability.
red_flags: Worker-side end-to-end handoff is not clearly shown in the frame sheet.
advance_reason: Highly original and WebMCP-native despite weaker live-demo verification.

one_line: A behavioral trust layer that compares WebMCP declarations with observed effects.
what_it_does: Classifies declared tool intent, observes network/storage/navigation effects, and flags mismatches before trusting a tool.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the security boundary being evaluated; observing whether a declared agent tool matches its actual browser effects is fundamentally dependent on the structured tool surface.
leverage_evidence: About text gives the Declare–Classify–Observe–Compare–Decide flow.
The malicious tool example attempts payment-like writes despite a harmless description.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent security prototype and multiple dark UI states, but the small frame evidence does not clearly demonstrate a complete verdict flow.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows dark trust/security screens, code-like output, and changing states.
About text specifies observation of network writes, storage mutations, and navigation.
impact_rationale: Misrepresented agent tools are a serious and directly relevant safety problem for the emerging agent-native web.
impact_evidence: About text gives a concrete payment-like malicious-tool scenario.
The product compares declared capabilities to browser-visible side effects.
creativity_rationale: Turning WebMCP’s intent declarations into a behavioral contract-testing and trust system is an original, ambitious response to a foundational risk.
creativity_evidence: The project builds and tests a lying tool rather than only discussing the threat.
Behavioral comparison is the central interaction model.
usability_note: Security concepts are clear in the description, but the visual prototype is dense and difficult to read.
red_flags: Frame text is largely illegible, limiting observed execution evidence.
advance_reason: Exceptional relevance and originality; execution is credible but less directly legible in the frames.

one_line: A governed goal room separating agent action, deterministic verification, and human acceptance.
what_it_does: Keeps plans, candidate bytes, evidence, verifier results, and owner approval distinct across a browser-local release workflow.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides narrow callable actions while the product adds shared state, evidence binding, and explicit authority boundaries that generic UI control would make harder to maintain.
leverage_evidence: About text describes six agent-callable tools with no privileged owner/system tools.
Goal Room binds owner acceptance to exact candidate bytes and visible evidence.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a particularly complete and internally consistent state machine, and frames show progression through goal entry, proposal, and contract review.
execution_evidence: Frames show goal creation, agent-proposed contract, and review states.
About text specifies deterministic FAIL/PASS, repair, exact-byte binding, sealed terminal state, and actor separation.
impact_rationale: It addresses a real governance problem for teams using agents to change software or operational artifacts: passing checks must not equal human approval.
impact_evidence: About text identifies stale state, wrong plan versions, and mismatched evidence as concrete failure modes.
Visible Goal Contract and review workflow support the stated problem.
creativity_rationale: The explicit separation of action, verification, and authority is a thoughtful and memorable interaction model for agent-mediated work.
creativity_evidence: PASS is visibly separated from approval.
Three actor roles and sealed terminal state are central to the design.
usability_note: The workflow is principled and inspectable but may feel complex for casual users.
advance_reason: Most complete governance workflow in the packet, with strong execution evidence.

one_line: An agent-friendly competitor monitoring service with zero-form signup and live change data.
what_it_does: Answers product and competitor questions, exposes tracked-company data, and starts a monitoring organization through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: The agent can query structured competitor data and create a provisional tracking setup without forms, while the human can continue from a claim link and token.
leverage_evidence: Eleven tools cover Q&A, company/industry/change data, and start_tracking_competitors.
About text describes zero-form setup, claim link, short-lived token, and follow-up change query.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a production-oriented, multilingual tool surface and frames show multiple product and interaction states, though successful signup confirmation is not clearly legible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows landing page, configuration/form states, and later interaction pages.
FACTS report live demo and 3 gallery images; about text specifies production and four languages.
impact_rationale: Competitor monitoring is a clear business need, and the service addresses missed updates with ongoing dated change feeds.
impact_evidence: About text identifies missed important competitor updates as the problem.
Stated dataset includes 300+ companies and a classified change feed.
creativity_rationale: The strongest originality is the no-account agent onboarding and claim handoff; competitor tracking itself is established.
creativity_evidence: Agent can establish monitoring before human ownership with a claim link.
Public data and Q&A tools are integrated into the same agent surface.
usability_note: The no-form setup is promising, but the frame collage is marketing-heavy and small text limits direct confirmation.
red_flags: Successful end-to-end signup/result is not clearly readable in the frames.
advance_reason: Strong practical fit and unusually complete agent onboarding concept.

one_line: A bridge that lets agents inspect pages and safely create new WebMCP tools at runtime.
what_it_does: Provides meta-tools for inspecting scope, proposing/registering tools, and executing one-off code with confirmation.
leverage_rationale: The agent is not merely consuming a fixed tool set; it dynamically assembles structured capabilities from the page, directly addressing the absence of WebMCP tools across the web.
leverage_evidence: Three meta-tools are named: inspect_page_scope, suggest_and_register_tool, and execute_code_mode.
About text describes discovering an existing filter function, asking permission, registering capability, and updating the live table/chart.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a complete, bounded demonstration with inspection, confirmation, execution, and visible data/chart change, though there is no public repository.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows world-data dashboard states, changing agent/object/task states, and tutorial explanation.
About text specifies confirmation before touching the page and four-row result above 7.4.
impact_rationale: It targets the real adoption bottleneck that most websites expose no agent tools, with a practical fallback for structured interaction.
impact_evidence: About text identifies empty document.modelContext surfaces on ordinary sites.
Demo scenario uses a real dashboard filter and updates table/chart through the app path.
creativity_rationale: Agent-authored, permissioned WebMCP tools are an exceptionally original and ambitious interpretation of runtime registration.
creativity_evidence: The product lets agents write the missing tools rather than waiting for every site author.
Safety confirmation and inspect-before-act are integral to the interaction model.
usability_note: Permissioned inspection is a good safety affordance, but dynamically authored tools could be demanding to explain.
red_flags: Dynamic code execution carries safety complexity even with confirmation.
standouts: Most novel WebMCP concept in the packet.
advance_reason: Transformative and clearly demonstrated agent capability assembly.

one_line: A shared planning workspace with live agent context, proposals, approvals, and human locks.
what_it_does: Lets agents analyze and propose plan changes while humans retain explicit approval and protected state in one workspace.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent structured access to the same live plan, focus context, dependencies, and locks, making collaboration more reliable than a separate chat copy.
leverage_evidence: About text describes five live tools, shared context, autonomy modes, and human-only restrictions.
Frames show dashboard, settings, activity timeline, and approval-oriented workflow screens.
execution_rationale: The product surfaces a coherent planning workflow with activity, settings, risk, proposals, and approval states; direct action completion is less visible than the surrounding UI.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows repeated workflow screens, five-tool caption, configuration states, and dashboard overview.
About text explicitly describes locked writes, medium-risk proposal, and approval/rejection controls.
impact_rationale: Teams have a real need to coordinate agent assistance without losing human control over priorities and risky plan changes.
impact_evidence: About text identifies duplicated context and unsafe autonomy as the problems.
Shared activity timeline and human-locked work are visible in the packet description.
creativity_rationale: The focus-as-context model and human-locked proposal workflow are a fresh synthesis of planning and agent governance.
creativity_evidence: Human focus becomes agent context in the shared workspace.
Agent proposals include before/after impact, risk, reasoning, and explicit decision controls.
usability_note: The dashboard and visible status model appear approachable, though governance adds workflow complexity.
red_flags: Frames emphasize UI states more than a fully legible end-to-end write-and-approval result.
advance_reason: Well-realized collaborative planning concept with strong human-control design.

one_line: A coloring studio where an agent turns children’s drawings into an interactive story stage.
what_it_does: Children draw and color characters, then a parent-directed agent places them in scenes and orchestrates movement, weather, and story actions.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP lets the agent read compact studio state and directly compose actions on the same canvas/stage, turning a static coloring activity into responsive collaborative play.
leverage_evidence: About text describes ten tools, get_guide, get_studio_state, and action-relevant context after writes.
Frame sheet shows progression from blank drawing canvas and tools to a finished sky/ground/character scene.
execution_rationale: The frames show a coherent color-to-play transformation with visible drawing controls, palette, canvas, and completed artwork; agent-directed movement itself is not fully legible in the contact sheet.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows drawing UI states and a completed illustrated scene.
About text specifies local artwork, state resync, guided choices, and play actions.
impact_rationale: It serves a specific family audience with a meaningful creative and imaginative use case, extending children’s own artwork rather than replacing it.
impact_evidence: About text centers parents and children and explicitly preserves child-created artwork.
Final frames show a completed character scene emerging from the studio.
creativity_rationale: The child-created drawing becoming an agent-directed story world is memorable, emotionally resonant, and deeply aligned with the medium.
creativity_evidence: Coloring and live storytelling are joined in one canvas/stage.
Agent offers choices rather than scripting the child’s play.
usability_note: The child/parent division and simple canvas tools are promising; agent setup remains parent-mediated.
red_flags: Agent choreography is described more strongly than it is visibly readable in the contact sheet.
standouts: Excellent transformation from drawing to play.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-impact creative use of shared agent/canvas state.

one_line: A voice-directed voxel island where a player and agent reshape the same live world.
what_it_does: Lets users request terrain, bridges, dominoes, characters, weather, and preview commerce while watching, interrupting, or undoing changes.
leverage_rationale: The agent needs structured live world state—terrain, position, actors, shops, camera, and recent changes—to enact and reverse high-level intentions reliably; pixel driving would be markedly inferior.
leverage_evidence: About text enumerates rich shared state and intention-level commands.
Frames show an isometric world changing, agent/character movement, overlays, task cards, and tutorial/toolbox explanation.
execution_rationale: The storyboard demonstrates a coherent playable world with changing map state, moving characters, placed objects, contextual overlays, task cards, and instructional framing, though voice interaction is not directly audible here.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows sequential island/world states, changing agent position, object appearance, popups, task cards, and tutorial transition.
About text specifies interrupt, redirect, and undo behaviors.
impact_rationale: It offers credible entertainment and creative sandbox value, with a compelling audience of players who want to shape worlds through intention rather than menus.
impact_evidence: Pitch and description define a playable voice-directed voxel world.
Visible settlement, buildable grid, characters, and contextual events demonstrate the play space.
creativity_rationale: A persistent voxel world that listens, transforms itself, and supports interruption, undo, and contextual commerce is unusually ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: High-level spoken intentions drive terrain, objects, weather, and characters.
The same world is shared by player and AI character over time.
usability_note: Direct intention commands and interrupt/undo are strong affordances, though a rich world may require careful onboarding.
red_flags: Commerce interactions are previews rather than real transactions.
Voice quality cannot be assessed from the transcript-free packet.
advance_reason: Exceptional ambition and WebMCP leverage with strong visible world-state evidence.
